Plotweaver

A data-in, chart-out studio built entirely from scratch — no D3, no Chart.js, no build step. You bring a table; Plotweaver draws every pixel.

Plotweaver is a single-page charting workbench with three live panels: an editable data grid on the left, a hand-written rendering canvas in the middle, and a configuration column on the right. Change anything in any panel and the chart updates immediately. The whole thing runs from static files — open index.html straight off disk and it works offline.

Real data editor

Edit cells inline, add or delete rows and columns, rename headers, and cycle a column's inferred type between number, date and string.

From-scratch renderer

Every chart is drawn with the Canvas 2D API. Nice-numbered axis ticks, gridlines, legends and hover tooltips are all hand-coded.

Real exports

Download a high-resolution PNG, a genuinely standalone SVG file, or a JSON bundle of the config plus data you can re-import later.

The charting engine

The renderer in js/chart.js turns a small view-model — { labels, series }, a list of { x, y } points, or a grid of values — into pixels. A few details that make the output trustworthy:

  • Nice-number axes. Tick values are chosen with the classic “nice numbers” algorithm so axes land on 1 / 2 / 5 × 10ⁿ boundaries instead of awkward decimals, regardless of the data range.
  • Honest auto-scaling. Each chart computes its own value extent — including stacked totals and negative values — and the baseline sits at zero whenever the data crosses it.
  • Crisp on any display. The canvas is sized for the device pixel ratio, so lines and text stay sharp on retina screens.
  • Calm motion. An optional entrance animation grows bars, sweeps pies and traces lines with an ease-out curve, and is automatically disabled when you prefer reduced motion.

Supported chart types

  • Bar — grouped or stacked, with rounded caps and per-series colors.
  • Line — multi-series with marker dots and column-wide hover.
  • Area — gradient fills, optionally stacked.
  • Scatter — X vs Y with an optional categorical grouping column for color.
  • Pie & Donut — percentage labels and a center total readout on the donut.
  • Radar — multi-axis spider chart comparing several series across attributes.
  • Heatmap — a color-graded matrix with in-cell values.
  • Histogram — automatic binning of a single numeric column.

Working with data

Load one of eight built-in datasets — SaaS revenue, global temperature, market sales, metro population, electricity mix, iris measurements, coffee cupping scores, or monthly rainfall — or paste your own. The CSV/TSV parser in js/data.js handles quoted fields, embedded commas and newlines, escaped quotes, and auto-detects whether your delimiter is a comma, tab or semicolon. It then infers each column's type so the chart can treat dates and numbers correctly.

Sharing & persistence

Your current dataset and chart configuration are saved to localStorage and also encoded into the page's URL hash. Hit Share to copy a link that reconstructs the exact chart — data and all — plus an <iframe> embed snippet. The gallery's “Open in studio” links use the same mechanism with a compact preset id.

Keyboard & accessibility

  • In the grid, Tab / Enter and the arrow keys move between cells.
  • Ctrl/Cmd + E exports the current chart as PNG.
  • Click any legend swatch to toggle that series on or off; the chart rescales to fit what remains.
  • Controls are focus-visible, the layout reflows to a tabbed single column on narrow screens, and all motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Plotweaver is a fictional product built as a self-contained demo. All datasets are hand-crafted to be realistic but illustrative.
